_comment: Individual source values reviewed by hand and found wrong. Keyed by food id; a nutrient set to null is dropped (missing beats wrong). Every entry says why. Applied after the automatic peer-outlier check (consumer/qa.py).

greek-yogurt-2-fat-plain-3b5a16._why: CNF 7469 lists 282.9 mg calcium per 100 g, likely a per-serving or entry error. Every other plain Greek yogurt across the 9 sources is 100-126 mg (strained yogurt loses calcium with the whey); set to the peer median, 115 mg, so the food doesn't count as zero.

soy-yogurt-plain-345e92._why: CNF 6987 lists 9.73 mg vitamin E and 45 mg vitamin C per 100 g. Every other soy yogurt across the sources is 0.2-0.3 mg vitamin E (CNF's own fruit and vanilla soy yogurts are 0.31) and 0-1 mg vitamin C unless fruit is added; set to the peer values so plain soy yogurt can't carry a day's vitamin E.

soba-noodles-dry-2dc785._why: Source F006043 lists 4.6 µg B12 per 100 g of dry soba. Buckwheat and wheat carry no B12, and every other soba record (USDA, MEXT) is 0; a vegan plan must not count it.

soba-noodles-boiled-343a44._why: Source F006042 lists 1.4 µg B12 per 100 g of boiled soba; same error as the dry record, every other soba record is 0.

perilla-egoma-oil-7638e7._why: The source record has total fat but no fatty-acid split, so the plan lab counted none of its saturated fat or omega-3. Perilla (egoma) oil is one of the richest ALA oils: published analyses put it at about 54-64% ALA, 12-18% linoleic acid, 13-18% oleic and 7-10% saturated fat. Set to the middle of those ranges.

tofu-medium-firm-prepared-with-calcium-s._why: CNF 3418 (from USDA SR 172476) lists 5.36 mg iron per 100 g, over three times every other tofu in the sources: CNF firm tofu 1.61, the Japanese tables 1.5 for firm and silken, and nine North American firm-tofu labels 1.2 to 2.0. Set to the label median, 1.6 mg, so a tofu-heavy week can't read 2 to 3 times its real iron.

natto-86df6e._why: The merged natto record carries 8.6 mg iron per 100 g (USDA SR). The Japanese Standard Tables (8th ed., 04046 itohiki natto, also in this library) give 3.3 mg, and natto's iron should sit near cooked soybeans of similar protein. Set to 3.3 mg, the value from the country that eats it daily.

soy-milk-all-flavors-enhanced-f9fdd1._why: The source has no phosphorus for fortified ('enhanced') soy drink, so every day using it was under-counted. Plain soy drink is about 45 to 50 mg per 100 g; fortified cartons add calcium as calcium carbonate or tricalcium phosphate, giving roughly 50 to 120 mg. Set to 90 mg, toward the high end, so upper-limit checks are never understated.

soybean-dry-roasted-bb3701._why: The source has no phosphorus, potassium or thiamin for dry-roasted soybeans. USDA SR 16111 (soybeans, mature seeds, dry roasted) lists 649 mg phosphorus, 1,364 mg potassium and 0.43 mg thiamin per 100 g.
